Subject: Dedicated capacity  integration & autoscaling next steps

Hi Samir 

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we all have the same context:

What we heard:
- Finlytics plans to move their production inference (chat + reranking + embeddings) to Redwood Dedicated for predictable latency and data isolation.
- Primary workloads: customer-chat (low-latency generation), nightly batch reranking (embeddings + reranker), and long-context document ingestion for retrieval ops.
- Initial target: sustain ~200 rps for chat with 95%-ile latency target of ~250ms token latency; peak bursts up to 600 rps for <10s bursts. Average request size ~60 tokens in, ~120 tokens out.

Open questions we asked you to confirm (please reply inline if possible):
1) Auth & network: will Finlytics use VPC peering + private routing or require an on-prem appliance? Any SAML/SCIM/IdP details we should prep for?
2) Expected concurrent user sessions (avg and peak)  you gave a rough 800 active users figure; can you map that to concurrent inference sessions?
3) Batch reranking cadence and QPS during re-ranks (approx qps and tokens per job).
4) Any hard constraints on cost vs latency tradeoffs (e.g., prefer cheaper quantized variants vs 95% latency SLO).

What Redwood will do next:
- Aditya will draft a first-pass Dedicated sizing + autoscaling policy based on the numbers above and the constrained burst behavior.
- Priyom will prepare an integration checklist covering SDK setup, auth patterns (mTLS/API keys/SSO), routing policies, and sample function-calling/structured-output snippets.
- I'll send a mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and a calendar invite for the deep-dive.

Attachments: please find a short Finlytics requirements worksheet you shared earlier attached for reference (finlytics_arch_requirements.pdf).

Next immediate step: Samir  can you confirm the three items above and share any load-test scripts or historical p95/p99 token latencies from your current infra? If yes, we can convert those into a sizing baseline.

Thanks  talk soon.

Hi Marissa 

Thanks for the clear recap. A few answers inline and additional context:

1) Auth & network: We prefer VPC peering into a dedicated subnet in our AWS account. We also require mTLS for server-to-server traffic and SAML-based SSO for console access. No on-prem appliance for the initial rollout.

2) Concurrent sessions: Of the ~800 active users, typical concurrent inference sessions are ~140 (chat sessions actively querying). Peak concurrency during US business hours can hit ~420 for short periods (30 60s) during support surges.

3) Batch reranking: Nightly jobs run two windows: 02:00 606:00 local time at ~150 qps with average 250 tokens per request; smaller rolling jobs throughout the day at 20 630 qps.

4) Cost vs latency: We prioritize latency for chat (95%-ile <= 300ms). For reranking, cost is more important than lowest latency and we are open to quantized model variants there.

I've attached the requirements doc we compiled (same as you have). I'll also share a small JMeter script we use for load testing after I clean it up  ETA end of day Monday.

Samir (and team) 

Thanks for the answers  helpful. Based on the numbers you shared I sketched a first-pass sizing + autoscaling approach and a short checklist for integration items below. This is a high-level recommendation; we'll refine after we see the load test.

First-pass Dedicated sizing (baseline assumptions):
- Chat workload: target sustained 200 rps, avg tokens total 180 (in+out), burst up to 600 rps for ~10s. 95%-ile latency target 250 6300ms per token.
- Reranker batch: 150 qps at 250 tokens (nightly)  cost-sensitive, can use 4-bit quantized model variant.

Rough capacity estimate:
- For the chat workload with the latency target, using our standard A100-equivalent instance profile, estimate: 6-8 GPUs with a small autoscaling buffer (scale-out at queue depth > 100ms sustained for 30s) to handle sustained + bursts when using continuous batching. For strict p95 latency, consider keeping a reserve pool (2 GPUs) for hot standby to absorb spikes without cold-starts.
- For batch rerankers: 1-2 GPU nodes using quantized model variant on a separate pool (lower priority routing).

Autoscaling policy (proposal):
- Metrics: request queue latency, GPU utilization, and prefix-KV cache hit rate.
- Scale-out: if request queue latency > 150ms OR GPU utilization > 75% for 45s, add 1 GPU.
- Scale-in: if GPU utilization < 40% AND queue latency < 50ms for 5m, remove 1 GPU.
- Warm-up: pre-warm new nodes by keeping a warm-cache instance (run a lightweight synthetic batch) before routing traffic.
- Burst policy: allow short burst capacity to exceed committed pool by routing to burst pool (pay-as-you-go) for <60s.

Queue sizing guidance:
- Keep request queue depth target under (N_gpus * 8) to limit visible latency amplification from queuing. Adjust constant based on observed per-GPU throughput.

Integration checklist (SDK/Auth/Routing/Tools):
- SDK: use our v2 SDK (node/python) with connection pooling and built-in backoff. We'll send sample snippet for token streaming + structured output (function-calling)  use the streaming endpoint for chat.
- Auth: mTLS for service-to-service; short-lived API tokens for app servers. SAML for console. We'll provide example cert rotation steps for mTLS.
- Routing: separate pools for chat (low-latency), reranker (cost-optimized); apply per-route model pinning and fallback rules.
- Structured output / function-calling: we'll share sample schema + tool-calling pattern to ensure deterministic parsing for your downstream systems.
- Embeddings/rerankers: use separate embedding index service; route embed requests to high-throughput pool and then fan-out to reranker pool for candidate scoring.

Next steps I need from you to firm this up:
- Confirm the peak burst characteristics (600 rps for 10s is our assumption).
- Share the load-test script or a short sample trace so we can run a mirrored load test against a staging pool.

I'll attach the quick sizing workbook (dedicated-sizing.xlsx) and will follow up with a more detailed node-by-node estimate after we get the test traces.
